name: Sofia: Returning novice preparing a first organised 5K

source.name: Sofia
source.label: Returning novice preparing a first organised 5K
source.health_context: Fictional, pain-free, no illness or medical rehabilitation. Future adaptation and event results are unknown.
source.training_history: Nine-month break, six weeks of consistent easy return; no previous organised race. Rep sets were submaximal observations, not max tests.
source.recovery_constraints: Recent longest run took 48 hours for normal leg recovery. Current movement and ordinary activity normal. No inferred race fitness from the training-paced 3 km.

mapping: Entirely new synthetic source facts authored before generation; no prescribed sessions or calendar assignments supplied.
Lift frequencies and strength visits are explicit athlete requests, not inferred from visit count.
Rep performances stay rep observations. Canonical UI estimatedMax supplies provisional loads, never a fabricated tested max.
Event permissions and whole-visit caps are explicit; no extra time, recovery clearance or readiness scores are invented.
The same canonical proposal/generator path supplies every prescription.

framework.rationale: Without a strength event, continue building rather than imposing a competition peak.

coachingInstructions.missedSession: Skip or move one session only if the next key session and recovery still fit. Do not stack missed quality, heavy work or long runs. After two missed sessions, illness or a week away, review the next block.
coachingInstructions.liftingEffort: Warm up to the prescribed effort. RPE governs the suggested kg. If effort overshoots by a point, reduce 2.5–5% and reassess; if still excessive, omit remaining back-offs. Heavy singles are skill practice, not forced maximal attempts.
coachingInstructions.speedWork: Accelerate with stable technique. Reduce load or stop when speed or position deteriorates. An easy speed day is not permission to turn it into a heavy day.
coachingInstructions.athleteJudgement: Report sustained fatigue, sleep disruption, pain, illness or altered movement. End the provoking work when needed. One difficult session is a reason to adjust that session, not an automatic full deload.
coachingInstructions.review: Review completed work every four weeks and after events. Later blocks are conditional on observed recovery and performance; no race result or lifting total is guaranteed.
